Ampere's law: the circulation of B around C equals mu_0 times the current through any surface bounded by C

Animation of Ampere's law with two surfaces bounded by the same curve. Two three-dimensional sketches side by side. In each, a closed curve C (a circle seen obliquely) is spanned by a tan-coloured surface that starts as the flat disc S1 and gradually bulges to the right into the dome S2 with the same rim. Left: a straight wire carrying a current I passes through the surface; the part of the wire inside the dome is drawn faintly and a red dot marks where it pierces the surface. The readout below says the current through the surface is I and the integral of B around C is mu_0 I, for S1, during the change, and for S2. Right: the wire comes in through the top, makes a U-turn and leaves through the bottom. It pierces the flat disc twice, once in and once out, so the net current through it is I - I = 0; as the surface bulges past the U-turn it is not pierced at all, so the current through it is 0. The integral of B around C is zero in both cases. The surfaces hold flat, then morph into domes over a few seconds, then hold; the readouts update as the piercing points move with the surface.
